appraisal_events.evidence: une personne presque du demi-monde, Mme de Crécy, que Mme Verdurin appelait par son petit nom, Odette, et déclarait être « un amour »; personnes ignorantes du monde... que si on leur avait offert de les faire inviter chez ces deux grandes dames, l'ancienne concierge et la cocotte eussent dédaigneusement refusé
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator situates Odette among the salon's reduced, marginal membership ("almost of the demi-monde") and worldly-naive followers easily duped about high society, so that Mme Verdurin's affectionate nickname is locally undercut by the ironic exposure of her narrow, credulous confinement to this minor circle.

appraisal_events.evidence: Si le docteur Cottard croyait devoir partir en sortant de table pour retourner auprès d'un malade en danger : « Qui sait, lui disait Mme Verdurin, cela lui fera peut-être beaucoup plus de bien que vous n'alliez pas le déranger ce soir »
appraisal_events.explanation: Mme Verdurin talks Cottard out of leaving to attend a patient in danger, locally positioning him as yielding his professional duty to the clan's social demands rather than asserting his own authority.

status_effects.explanation: Framed as "almost of the demi-monde" and worldly-naive, she is locally diminished in sophistication and standing despite Mme Verdurin's affectionate label.
His medical duty toward a patient is subordinated to Mme Verdurin's social pressure, showing him yielding professional autonomy to the clan's authority.

ambiguities: Whether docteur Cottard actually complies with Mme Verdurin's dissuasion and stays rather than attending his patient is not confirmed by the passage; the effect on his professional standing is implied rather than stated as a concrete outcome.

Le pianiste and le peintre also receive extravagant praise/patronage from Mme Verdurin (e.g., 'enfonçait' Planté et Rubinstein), but this is treated as part of the already-captured Credo/cult dynamic (accepted E1) rather than a distinct outcome of their own, so they were omitted.
